problem: known hazard: "Estudio en la universidad" is just the term plus a verb, reads as the answer itself
example: Mi hermana estudia en la universidad nueva.
exampleEn: My sister studies at the new university.

problem: known hazard: "La puerta de embarque es la doce" only names the term, no context
example: La puerta de embarque abre en quince minutos.
exampleEn: The boarding gate opens in fifteen minutes.

problem: wrong be-verb: location needs estar, not "es en el pasillo"
example: Mi asiento está en el pasillo.
exampleEn: My seat is on the aisle.

problem: unnatural without an intensifier: "el precio es alto" reads as a dictionary line
example: El precio de la carne es muy alto.
exampleEn: The price of meat is very high.

problem: idiom: "un descuento grande" should be "un gran descuento" before the noun
exampleEn: They gave me a big discount.

problem: near-duplicate: "Soy estudiante todavía" is the term with two filler words
example: Mi primo es estudiante en Madrid.
exampleEn: My cousin is a student in Madrid.

problem: known hazard: "El examen es el viernes" is the term plus a bare date
example: El examen de historia es el viernes.
exampleEn: The history exam is on Friday.

problem: known hazard: "Me duele la cabeza" is literally the term's gloss (headache) with nothing else
example: El niño se golpeó la cabeza con la puerta.
exampleEn: The boy hit his head on the door.

problem: known hazard: "Tengo la nariz tapada" is just the stock collocation for the term
example: Tengo la nariz roja del frío.
exampleEn: My nose is red from the cold.

problem: definition-flavored generic sentence that mirrors the term instead of using it
example: Me late muy rápido el corazón cuando corro.
exampleEn: My heart beats very fast when I run.
